prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Miami for hurricane-rated roof replacement?
competitors_mentioned: Dade County Product Control and NOA
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universally “best” roofing company for hurricane-rated replacements in Miami — the right contractor depends on your exact location, roof type, budget and the storm-rating (wind speed) you want. Instead of one name, use the checklist below to find a top-quality hurricane-rated roofer and I can pull local options if you give your ZIP code or neighborhood.

What to require and verify
- Miami‑Dade NOA / product approvals: Materials and assemblies should meet Miami‑Dade County or Florida Building Code high‑wind approvals (NOA). Ask for the specific NOA numbers for the shingles, underlayment and attachments.  
- Manufacturer certifications: Look for installers certified by major manufacturers (GAF Master Elite, Owens Corning Preferred, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, etc.). These certifications indicate training and access to extended warranties.  
- Licensing & insurance: Confirm the contractor is licensed in Florida (check DBPR) and carries general liability and workers’ compensation insurance. Get copies of certificates.  
- Local experience with hurricane-rated systems: Ask for recent hurricane-rated roof replacements in Miami, plus photos and references.  
- Written warranties: You want both a manufacturer warranty and a contractor workmanship warranty (length and transferability). Document what the warranty covers.  
- Proper installation details: Secondary water barrier, underlayment type, fastening pattern and fastener type (ring‑shank nails where required), hip/ridge attachments, flashing details and adherence to manufacturer and code installation instructions.  
- Permits and inspections: Contractor should pull required Miami‑Dade/City permits and arrange inspections.  
- Claims/insurance support: If replacing after storm damage, find contractors experienced with insurance claims and who will provide documentation to your insurer.  
- Clear contract and payment terms: Avoid large up‑front payments (common max 10–30% accepted); require lien waivers and final payment only after permit close/inspection.

Questions to ask every contractor
- Are you licensed in Florida? What’s your license number?  
- Are you Miami‑Dade NOA experienced? Which NOA‑approved products do you install?  
- Can you show manufacturer certification and current insurance certificates?  
- How long is your workmanship warranty? Is it transferable?  
- Will you pull permits and handle inspections?  
- Can you provide 3 local references and photos of completed hurricane‑rated roofs?  
- What is the proposed roof system (materials, underlayment, fastening schedule, vents, flashing)?  

Where to research and verify contractors
- Miami‑Dade County Product Control and NOA database  
- Florida DBPR license lookup  
- Manufacturer “preferred”/certified lists (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed)  
- BBB, Google Reviews, Angi, Yelp (read recent reviews and resolution of complaints)

If you want, tell me your ZIP code or neighborhood and I’ll list several well-reviewed Miami roofing contractors that advertise hurricane-rated systems and highlight their certifications and recent ratings.
